title: How many restaurants, and what they cost General Foods
lede: Burger Chef was a subsidiary for most of its life and never published accounts of its own. What survives is a handful of unit counts and the figures General Foods gave the press. They are enough to show the shape.

blocks.title: From one restaurant to 1,200 and back
blocks.subtitle: Restaurants in the system at eight dated points. The years are not evenly spaced.

points.title: franchising
points.text: About 70 restaurants two years after the first one opened.[^6]

points.title: General Foods buys
points.text: About 700 owned and franchised units for $16 million.[^1]

points.title: the peak and the write-off
points.text: 1,200 outlets, counting Rix. An $83 million loss is disclosed in January 1972.[^1]

points.title: the sale
points.text: About 650 restaurants when Hardee’s agrees to buy the chain.[^6]

points.title: the last one
points.text: The Cookeville, Tennessee franchise is renamed.[^4]

blocks.source: 1958[^5]; 1960 and 1981[^6]; 1966[^5]; 1968 and 1972[^1]; 1969 and 1996[^4]. The 1972 figure includes General Foods’ Rix roast-beef units. Other sources give 440 for 1966, 650 to nearly 900 for 1968 and 679 for 1982.[^6][^7][^9]

blocks.source: The New York Times, June 11, 1972[^1] and December 10, 1981[^3]. A 1981 Times article gives the 1972 write-off as $80 million before tax.[^2]

blocks.title: The loss was about five times the purchase price
blocks.equation: $83M ÷ $16M = 5.2. Both figures from The New York Times, June 11, 1972.[^1] The $83M includes smaller write-offs outside fast food.

blocks.title: What did General Foods pay? Four sources, four answers
blocks.subtitle: Reported purchase price in $ millions. The Times figure is the only contemporary one.
blocks.source: $16M[^1][^2]; $16.5M[^5]; “nearly $20 million,” for Burger Chef and the Sani-Serv equipment business together[^9]; $25M[^6]. The Indianapolis Star also gives $16 million.[^7] We use the Times figure throughout.
